findings.description: The key-verify publish step's 3-attempt retry loop cannot actually retry — a latent deviation from the proven fleet pattern that this delivery activates. On a push race (origin moves every few minutes), attempt 1's failure handler runs 'git checkout -- .' + 'git reset --hard origin/main', which wipes the receipt content from the working tree (receipts/key-check.json and key-check-log.jsonl exist at HEAD with old content, so the files revert to the 2026-09-18 Console-era receipt). Attempt 2 then stages nothing new and 'git commit' exits 1 ('nothing to commit') under bash -e — the step goes red and the verdict receipt is lost (the verdict remains visible in the run log; on the armed path the vault write + grid dispatch already happened before publish). The proven fleet pattern (money-watch, moment-watch, agents-watch) re-runs its generator inside the loop after the reset ('node agents/…mjs' — verified 2 occurrences in each); key-verify has no regeneration line (1 occurrence only — the verify step). The earlier fleet-inspect audit (8cb6f20, finding E3) moved add+commit inside the loops but key-verify was dormant then and never received the generator re-run.
findings.requiredFix: Add regeneration inside the loop — 'node agents/key-verify.mjs' after the reset (the money-watch pattern; on the armed path a re-run repeats an idempotent sealed-box PUT and one extra grid dispatch, harmless per the r68 atomic-grid note) — or replace the hard reset with 'git reset --soft origin/main' so the receipt stays staged for the next commit. Until fixed: a publish race = honest red + verdict in the run log + re-dispatch; acceptable to ship, fix in the same or next delivery.
